newsitem.title: CHINA: China completes 69.68 pct of planned T-bond offer.
newsitem.headline: China completes 69.68 pct of planned T-bond offer.

text.p: China had issued 85.712 billion yuan ($10.326 billion) worth of certificate bonds as of June 3, completing 69.68 percent of the planned total offer, the official media said on Monday.
China has set a total offer of 123 billion yuan worth of certificate type non-tradeable treasury bonds to be issued between March 1 and October 20.
The state offer consists of 25 billion yuan worth of two-year debt, as well as 73 billion yuan in three-year and 25 billion yuan in five-year debt.

As of June 3, a total of 22.238 billion yuan of two-year debt was sold as well as 49.794 billion yuan of three-year debt and 13.68 billion of five-year debt, the Beijing Economic Daily newspaper said.

The sale of state debt slowed somewhat from last year because of rising corporate debt issues, which carry 11 percent interest for a three-year maturity compared with 9.18 percent on a comparable treasury offer.
A strong stock market has also lured funds away from the bond market, the newspaper said.
